action: Infoblox customers: no specific action yet. Watch for a direct notice from the company on whether your information is involved, and be careful with unexpected emails that claim to come from Infoblox.
date_note: Disclosed this week; exact day not confirmed
exec: A security vendor's data was exposed through a supplier; scope is unknown, so customer impact cannot yet be judged.
plain: Network security company Infoblox confirmed that someone got unauthorised access to company information through an outside firm it used to move data. What was accessed has not been detailed.

sources.name: Security Affairs (relaying The Register and TechCrunch)

summary: Infoblox told TechCrunch it is investigating unauthorized access to company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor, and sees no indication its products, cloud services, updates or build processes were involved. Security Affairs, citing The Register, reports staff data (including Social Security numbers) and some customer NIOS configuration snapshots were taken; Infoblox has not confirmed scope or numbers.
title: Infoblox confirms company data accessed through a migration vendor

validation.note: TechCrunch (Infoblox spokesperson statement) and Security Affairs read; Security Affairs relays The Register's anonymous-source and CEO-email claims, which Infoblox has not confirmed. Original Register article not read.

review.note: Added TechCrunch with the Infoblox spokesperson statement; summary now says no products involved and data theft is one anonymous source
